title: The Biggest No. 2 Hot 100 Hits of All Time
summary: Though they fell short of the Hot 100's top spot, some No. 2 hits have generated cultural legacies that rival or even eclipse their chart-topping competition.
contentText:
In his autobiography Q , Quincy Jones wrote, “Numbers 2, 6, and 11 are my least-favorite chart positions.” It doesn’t take a Jones-like genius to determine why. Despite a clear vote of public favor, each song that peaks at those ranks can come with a pang of disappointment as a song’s creators and performers just miss out on forever claiming a No. 1, top five or top 10 hit.

Yet, particularly with No. 2-peaking hits, many of those narrow misses have evolved into iconic tracks with pop-culture legacies that rival or even eclipse their contemporary competition. Some – including a case a few years ago – sustain enough momentum to leapfrog No. 1 hits and become the year’s top Hot 100 single, others provide a springboard of momentum for artists to eventually capture that chart-topping hit on a subsequent try, and a select few dominate pop culture so strongly that you’d swear that they definitely, surely, undoubtedly topped the chart – before the facts reveal otherwise.

While the No. 1s get plenty of shine, let’s celebrate another slate of hit singles that deserve a moment in the spotlight. Here is Billboard ’s official countdown of the top 50 songs to peak at No. 2 on the Hot 100.

Billboard’s Biggest No. 2 Hits recap ranking is based on weekly performance on the Hot 100 through Aug. 15, 2026, with eligibility limited to songs that peaked at No. 2 and excluding holiday tracks that have seasonal returns to the chart. Songs are ranked based on an inverse point system, with weeks at No. 1 earning the greatest value and weeks at lower spots earning the least. Due to changes in chart methodology over the years, eras are weighted differently to account for chart turnover rates during various periods.
